lanes.title: two-level morale: victory raises morale (D-082 DA1, DA2), research and prototype
lanes.brief: SCOPE LIMITS: work only in prototypes/m7-sprint1 (M7Proto.slnx; M7Econ.slnx only if economy code is touched) and docs/m7-plan; no change to Sim.Core, Sim.Data, Sim.Cli, Sim.Ui or their tests, no unit data or cap change, no permanent project, no CI change (D-079 §6, Q5 open). Every design document is marked PROPOSAL; every reading is labelled READING with both alternatives; no Director decision is invented or reopened. Read docs/d082-morale-caps-ties-director-answers-2026-11-10.md in full first (the Director's message of 2026-11-10, DA1-DA9, its readings DA1-R..DA8-R, §3 supersessions, §5 not decided). (1) RESEARCH (DA2; reference only under D-069 and docs/ip-originality.md: our own design, numbers, names and text; nothing player-facing names another game). Research how the Director's reference game (named in D-082 DA2) handles morale at two levels: the army's morale on the campaign map (does an army-wide morale exist; what raises and lowers it: victories, defeats, supplies, attrition, leaders, events; how it carries into battle) and each unit's morale in battle (what raises and lowers it: casualties total and recent, flank and rear attacks, missile fire, the commander's presence, death or wounding of commanders and heroes, nearby friendly routs, winning or losing its own fight, the battle's overall balance, fatigue, ambush, fear; the states up to rout; rallying; shattering; how a won or lost battle feeds back to the campaign). Use WebSearch and WebFetch; the session's network policy denies some hosts (totalwar.fandom.com and gamepur.com were denied on 2026-11-10): try others once, never retry a denied host, and say which hosts were denied. Label every claim [CODE] (read in game files or scripts), [SEARCH] (a search summary or a fetched page, with its URL) or [KNOW] (unverified knowledge), and say plainly what could not be verified; do not invent mechanics. Compare briefly with two or three other strategy and tactics games' morale models as genre patterns. (2) DESIGN PROPOSAL docs/m7-plan/morale-proposal.md (our own design; the research goes in a labelled reference annex): (a) unit (formation) morale in battle, starting from what the prototype TacticalResolver and AutoResolver already do (BattleSetup.cs MoraleMax, HoldRecovery 20, RallyRecovery 60; TacticalBattle.Domain.cs:870; AutoResolver.cs:817; casualty-driven loss; rout) and saying what, if anything, should change, for example a rise for winning the local fight; (b) army morale on the campaign (lane E's WarEconomyWorld morale in micro units, its pulse-end recovery and hunger and arrears penalties, reports/H-E.md; lane D's SupportMath.MoraleAfterBattle and SetMoraleAfterBattle, docs/m7-plan/support-capabilities-proposal.md §3.3): the after-battle change becomes DR29's decrease through combat plus DA1's rise for the winning side (DA1-R (a): the winner's participating formations and their army); say whether the loser takes an extra defeat penalty (PROPOSAL); (c) how the two levels feed each other (campaign morale into the battle's start morale, the M7.15 hand-off; the battle's outcome back to the army); (d) what counts as a win, from the outcomes the resolvers report (routed, retreated, surrendered, eliminated), with DA6 and DA7 (equal sides go to the defender, an ambush to the ambusher under DA7-R (a)); lane AP will implement DA6/DA7 in the AutoResolver later, so use the reported winner and say so; (e) Law 2: the victory rise is a change of a morale stock that then recovers or decays toward a baseline at per-sim-year rates integrated with dtYears, never a free-floating permanent buff; Law 3 dt-correctness; Law 5 determinism (integer micro units, no float); (f) READING M (b), whether taking part alone costs morale, stays OPEN: present it, do not decide it. (3) PROTOTYPE: replace lane D's 'a battle never raises the campaign morale' rule with the DA1 rule for the winning side (keep DR29's decrease for every participant), and implement any unit-morale change the proposal adopts in the prototype resolvers. Semantic tests per rule (the winner rises, the loser falls, a battle won on equal sides raises the defender's morale, an ambush win raises the ambusher's), exact integer arithmetic, turn-exact pins where a rule applies at an instant, tie-dense ordering tests where ordering matters, POPULATED-table round-trip tests for any new serialized row, bounded mutants each killed by a semantic test. Every moved golden or pin gets a measured attribution; lane D's morale tests change only where DA1 supersedes them (say which). (4) Lane report prototypes/m7-sprint1/reports/H-MOR.md: research provenance, the design, readings, decisions for the Director (only genuinely undecided ones, each with alternatives), MEASURED vs INFERRED, tests, mutants, what ran, NOT RUN and deferred. Builds and tests: M7Proto.slnx (and M7Econ.slnx if touched) in Debug and Release, prototypes/m7-sprint1/scripts/check-proto-determinism.sh, python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py --all.
